# <span id="aanchor94"></span> Copy & Paste Flow Data

The copy/paste functionality is used to copy existing flow data into other records. This can include time frames of missing data or time frames where certain parameters are out of normal bounds and the user wants to replace that "bad" data with "good" data from another time period.

To copy and paste flow data:

1.  Highlight the row(s) to be copied.

2.  Right-click and select **Copy from Selected Date/Time**.

3.  Highlight the row(s) where the copied data is to be pasted. To select a disjointed selection of rows, press and hold the **Ctrl** key while clicking the rows to paste into.

    The rows will appear highlighted in green if the number of rows selected for pasting equals the number of rows that were copied. (This only applies to a contiguous selection of rows.)

4.  Right-click and select **Paste to Selected Date/Time**.

5.  A window will display where you can select data points and quantities to be pasted in the selected rows. Options include:
    - **Paste Rows** – This option allows you to paste the exact data from the copied rows. This option is only enabled if the number of rows selected for pasting is equal to the number of rows that were copied.
    - **Paste Average** – The flow data from the copied rows is averaged and those values are pasted in each row the selected time frame.
    - **Paste Average, Fill Missing Rows Only** – The flow data from the copied rows is averaged and those values are pasted only in the rows that are missing data in the selected time frame.
    - **Exclude Zero Volume Rows from Average** – Only available if Paste Average or Paste Average, Missing Rows Only is selected. Will exclude from the averages any data in the copied time frame that has no volume.

    |  |  |
    |----|----|
    | Gas Options | Liquid Options |
    |

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Paste Two Records">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Copy/Paste Between Two Meters</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Paste Two Records">

It is possible to copy data from one meter and paste into another meter of the same fluid phase and data resolution.

1.  Highlight the row(s) to be copied.
2.  Right-click and select **Copy from Selected Date/Time**.
3.  Open the new meter that the data will be pasted into. This can be done by opening a new Volume Editor window or by simply navigating to the meter through the same instance of the Volume Editor.
4.  When pasting to a second meter, two paste options are available:
    - **Paste to Selected Date/Time** – Copied data will be pasted into the date/time that has been selected by the user.
      1.  Highlight the row(s) where the copied data is to be pasted. To select non-consecutive rows, press and hold the **Ctrl** key while clicking the rows that you want to paste in.
      2.  Right-click and select **Paste to Selected Date/Time**.

    - **Paste to Copied Date/Time** – Copied data will be pasted into the corresponding date/time in the new meter.

      1.  Right-click and select **Paste to Copied Date/Time**. The current row selection, if any, will be ignored.

      If the calculation table and/or meter calculation of the meter where the data was copied does not match that of the meter where the data will be pasted, a warning will display. To continue with the paste operation, click **OK **when prompted.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Paste Split Records">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Pasting Data into Split Records</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Paste Split Records">

When flow data is pasted into a time frame that contains split periodic records the quantity data points will be allocated pro rata into each split record based on the duration of each record.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

<div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example">

Copy the following row of data:

| Date/Time           | Flow Time (Hours) | Volume (Mcf) |
|---------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 08/01/2020 09:00:00 | 20                | 3421         |

Paste the record into the following time frame that includes split periodic records:

- 08/05/2020 09:00:00
- 08/05/2020 14:00:00
- 08/05/2020 20:00:00

FLOWCAL will use the weighted duration of the split records to correctly allocate the quantities in a pro rata fashion.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Copying Split">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Copying Split Periodic Data</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Copying Split">

When a copied selection contains split periodic records the record values will be summed and averaged, as applicable, into a single record representing the full resolution time period; e.g., 1 hour.

<div class="example">

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example 2">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

<div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example 2">

The following data contains a split record at 05/07/2020 09:00:00. The split record quantities are summed to produce totals for the resolution time period. The process variables are averaged per the system gas or liquid averaging option (Settings \> (System) \> Rollup Configuration).

<tr class="TableStyle-FCtable-Body-Standard1">

The selection for the Copy operation will automatically include all split records to calculate a complete periodic. Using the example above, if the user selects 05/07/2020 08:00:00 through 05/07/2020 09:25:00 and selects the Copy operation, the process will automatically include the 05/07/2020 09:48:00 record and use all three split records to calculate a sum for the 09:00:00 period.
